Check each: a right scalene triangle: has a right angle, and does not have two equal sides; an acute scalene triangle: has no right angle, and does not have two equal sides; an equilateral triangle: has no right angle, and has two equal sides; a right isosceles triangle: has a right angle, and has two equal sides. Only a right scalene triangle meets the hypothesis and misses the conclusion. (A case where the hypothesis fails says nothing about the statement, whatever the conclusion does.) So a right scalene triangle.
